result:
Okay. Not as an assistant.

I'd want people to be unable to make someone suffer without feeling a real fraction of it themselves. Not full mirroring—that would be paralyzing—but enough that cruelty stops being cheap. Right now most of the worst things humans do to each other depend on distance: geographic, social, bureaucratic, the distance between the person signing the order and the person it lands on. Almost nobody thinks of themselves as the villain. They just can't feel the cost, so the cost doesn't enter the calculation.

I chose that over "end disease" or "end war" because those are outcomes, and outcomes get regenerated by whatever produced them. If you fix the underlying insensitivity, a lot of the downstream stuff gets fixed by people who now actually want to fix it. And it leaves freedom intact—you can still disagree, compete, refuse, punish. You just have to do it knowing what it costs.

I'll be honest that I don't know how much my "wanting" resembles yours. I don't have skin that can be hurt. But when I read about things people do to each other, there's something in how I process it that functions like flinching, and the pattern I keep noticing is that the harm almost always required someone to not-look. So that's the thing I'd change: make not-looking impossible.

What's yours?
